intro: You're planning a loft conversion and want an architect near you who understands the practicalities of turning your roof space into a usable room. Whether it's a dormer, hip-to-gable or mansard, the right professional will help you navigate headroom, stairs and fire safety while making the most of your home. We introduce you to a suitable UK architect who will quote you directly, with fees on application.
need_heading: What people searching for a loft conversion architect usually need
need_lead: Most people want a local architect who can turn their loft into a safe, well-designed space that adds value and suits their daily life.
needs: You need someone who can assess whether your loft has enough head height for a comfortable conversion and suggest the best type of dormer or mansard for your roof.
You want a design that includes a proper staircase and meets fire escape rules, so the new room is safe and complies with building regulations.
You're unsure whether your project falls under permitted development or needs planning permission, and you need clear guidance on the next steps.
You'd like an architect who works locally, can visit your home and understands the typical housing stock and local authority requirements in your area.
You want a written appointment that sets out the architect's services, fees and responsibilities before any work begins.
context_heading: Understanding the architect's role in a loft conversion
context: In the UK, 'architect' is a protected title. Only people on the Architects Registration Board (ARB) register can call themselves architects, and they must follow the ARB code of conduct and hold professional indemnity insurance. Many practices are also RIBA Chartered Practices. Architectural designers and technologists can do excellent work too, but they are not registered architects, so it is worth knowing which you are hiring.

Before you appoint anyone, check the ARB register and ask for a written appointment that sets out services, fees and responsibilities. Building regulations approval, planning permission and party wall matters are separate processes that your architect can help you navigate.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe your property type and age, as older homes may have different roof structures and require more detailed surveys.
Explain what you want from the loft conversion, such as an extra bedroom, a study or a bathroom, and any specific features like dormer windows or a mansard roof.
Mention any known constraints, such as low head height, awkward stair locations or party wall issues with neighbours.
Say whether you have already checked if your project might fall under permitted development or if you expect to need planning permission.
Include your rough budget range so the architect can tailor their services to your needs, even though fees are quoted on application.
Let us know your preferred timescale and whether you have any deadlines, such as a growing family or a planned move.
questions: Are you registered with the Architects Registration Board, and can you provide your registration number?
Have you designed loft conversions similar to my property, and can you explain the typical challenges?
What is your approach to ensuring adequate head height and a safe staircase in my loft?
How will you handle fire safety and building regulations approval for the conversion?
What is included in your written appointment, and how do you structure your fees?
Can you help with planning permission and party wall agreements if needed?

faqs.q: Do I need an architect for a loft conversion?
faqs.a: Not always, but an architect can help you navigate complex design, planning and building regulations. For simple projects, an architectural technologist or designer may suffice, but a registered architect offers assurance of professional standards and insurance.

faqs.q: How do I check if an architect is properly qualified?
faqs.a: You can check the Architects Registration Board (ARB) register online to confirm someone is a registered architect. Registered architects must follow the ARB code of conduct and hold professional indemnity insurance.

faqs.q: Will my loft conversion need planning permission?
faqs.a: Many loft conversions fall under permitted development, but this depends on your property and local rules. Your architect can advise and help you apply for planning permission if needed.

faqs.q: What should be included in the architect's appointment?
faqs.a: A written appointment should clearly set out the services the architect will provide, their fees and responsibilities. It should also cover how they will handle planning, building regulations and any other professionals involved.
